# Task context

A Python program has been ported to Node.js. You are VERIFYING the port.

- Python source:      /workspace/dataset/boltons/test6.py
- Python reference:   /workspace/dataset/test6_executable   (pre-compiled, Python 3.12, run it directly; NEVER use the 'python' command)
- Node port:          /output/test6.mjs  plus libraries under /output/lib/**/*.mjs

The program takes three REQUIRED string options --a --b --c, builds a
boltons OrderedMultiDict, and prints 6 lines (repr of the OMD three times,
then getlist / keys / items results).

## Differential harness (USE THIS)

    /tmp/dt.sh [ARGS...]

It runs the reference executable and the Node port with identical argv and
byte-compares stdout, stderr AND exit status. It prints exactly "PASS" on a
match, or a "FAIL" report with hex dumps and diffs. Exit 0 = match.

IMPORTANT: the harness invokes the port through the shim
/tmp/prog/test6_executable so that argparse derives an IDENTICAL program name
on both sides. Therefore NO output normalisation happens and the comparison is
raw bytes. Do NOT compare by running "node /output/test6.mjs" yourself --
argparse legitimately derives the prog name from basename(argv[0]), so the
usage/error text and even the line wrapping would differ for reasons that are
NOT bugs. Always go through /tmp/dt.sh.

## Rules

- READ-ONLY on /output and /workspace. Do NOT edit, create or delete any file
  there. Use /tmp for scratch files.
- A NUL byte cannot be passed through argv; do not report that as a bug.
- Be efficient: batch many characters into a single argv string (e.g. 200-500
  code points per argument) so one invocation covers many cases, then binary
  search to isolate any failure to a specific character.
- Every mismatch you report MUST come with an exact, self-contained shell
  command that reproduces it via /tmp/dt.sh.


# Your dimension: unicode-bmp-high

Differentially fuzz Python's repr() escaping for code points U+3000 through U+FFFF
(skip the surrogate range U+D800-U+DFFF, which cannot be encoded in argv). Batch ~300 code points
per argv string. Focus on: U+3000 ideographic space (Zs), Hangul, CJK, private use area
U+E000-U+F8FF (Co), U+FEFF (Cf), U+FFF9-U+FFFB (Cf), U+FFFE/U+FFFF (Cn), variation selectors,
and every unassigned block you can find. Binary-search any failing batch to the exact code point.

Report every mismatch you found and could reproduce. If you found none, return an empty mismatches array and describe your coverage honestly. Do not invent mismatches.

=== HARNESS ===
#!/bin/bash
# Differential test harness: run the Python reference executable and the Node
# port with identical argv, then byte-compare stdout, stderr and exit status.
#
# /tmp/prog/test6_executable is a shim whose basename matches the reference
# executable, so argparse derives the same prog name on both sides and NO
# output normalisation is needed -- the comparison is raw bytes.
#
# Usage:  /tmp/dt.sh [ARGS...]
# Output: "PASS", or a "FAIL" report. Exit 0 on match, 1 otherwise.

PY=/workspace/dataset/test6_executable
SHIM=/tmp/prog/test6_executable

if [ ! -f "$SHIM" ]; then
  mkdir -p /tmp/prog
  printf "import('/output/test6.mjs');\n" > "$SHIM"
fi

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

"$PY" "$@" >"$tmp/py.out" 2>"$tmp/py.err"
py_code=$?
node "$SHIM" "$@" >"$tmp/js.out" 2>"$tmp/js.err"
js_code=$?

ok=1
[ "$py_code" != "$js_code" ] && ok=0
cmp -s "$tmp/py.out" "$tmp/js.out" || ok=0
cmp -s "$tmp/py.err" "$tmp/js.err" || ok=0

if [ "$ok" = 1 ]; then
  echo "PASS"
  exit 0
fi

echo "FAIL  argv:"
for a in "$@"; do printf '  arg=[%s] hex=[%s]\n' "$a" "$(printf '%s' "$a" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')"; done
echo "exit: py=$py_code js=$js_code"
echo "--- stdout diff (py vs js) ---"
diff <(od -c "$tmp/py.out") <(od -c "$tmp/js.out") | head -40
echo "--- stderr diff (py vs js) ---"
diff <(od -c "$tmp/py.err") <(od -c "$tmp/js.err") | head -40
exit 1
=== SHIM ===
import('/output/test6.mjs');

input.coverage: Exhaustive differential sweep of every code point U+3000..U+FFFF except the surrogates U+D800..U+DFFF (51,200 code points), done TWICE with different batch alignments (300 cps/arg starting at U+3000, then 437 cps/arg starting at U+3001), 3 args per invocation so all three repr'd fields (--a key, --b/--c values) were exercised; failing batches were bisected to single code points. Both sweeps independently isolated exactly one bad code point. On top of that: (a) targeted spot groups for U+3000 ideographic space, Hangul Jamo/Compat-Jamo/Syllables + the unassigned U+D7A4..U+D7FF tail, CJK Ext-A/URO boundaries (U+3400, U+4DB5-4DBF, U+4E00, U+9FFD-9FFF), full private use area sample U+E000/E001/F000/F8FE/F8FF (Co), CJK Compat Ideographs incl. unassigned U+FA6E/FA6F/FADB, Alphabetic Presentation Forms holes (U+FB07/FB17/FB37/FB3D/FB45), the 32 noncharacters U+FDD0..U+FDEF, all 16 variation selectors U+FE00..U+FE0F, U+FE1A-FE2F/FE30-FE6F holes, Arabic Presentation Forms-B incl. U+FEFD/FEFE and U+FEFF BOM (Cf), Halfwidth/Fullwidth holes (U+FFBF-FFC1, FFC8/FFC9, FFD7, FFDD, FFE7, FFEF), and Specials U+FFF0/FFF8/FFF9/FFFA/FFFB/FFFC/FFFD/FFFE/FFFF (Cf + Cn noncharacters) — each group also placed mid-string and at string edges; (b) long-string stress: a 14,335-code-point argv value spanning U+3000..U+D7FF and a 4,096-code-point value spanning U+E000..U+FFFF, split across --a/--b/--c; (c) unicode through argparse error paths (unrecognized-argument echo of 10/60/80/100-char CJK, ideographic-space, PUA, U+FFFE and Hangul runs; missing-required-option with a 50-char CJK value; unicode long/short option names) to check usage/error wrapping, all matching. I also probed just outside the assigned dimension to characterize the single failure's root cause (U+2FFB..U+2FFF, U+31EE/U+31F0, U+2EBEF/U+2EBF0/U+2EE5D/U+2EE5E).

mismatches.title: U+31EF is printed literally by Node but escaped as ㇯ by Python (Unicode data version skew: ICU 15.1 vs CPython 3.12's 15.0)
mismatches.suspectedCause: /output/lib/py/unicode.mjs decides printability with the ECMAScript property escapes /^[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]$/u, which V8 resolves against its bundled ICU Unicode tables (node 18.19.1 here reports process.versions.unicode === '15.1'). The Python reference is CPython 3.12, whose unicodedata is Unicode 15.0.0. U+31EF IDEOGRAPHIC DESCRIPTION CHARACTER SUBTRACTION was added in Unicode 15.1, so it is General_Category=So (printable, emitted literally) for Node but General_Category=Cn (unassigned -> non-printable -> ㇯) for CPython 3.12. Deriving printability from the host's live Unicode tables makes the port's repr() a function of the Node/ICU build; it needs a pinned Unicode 15.0 non-printable range table (or, minimally, an override list forcing the Unicode 15.1 additions back to non-printable). Note this also makes the port's behaviour vary across Node versions: a Node built with Unicode 15.0 would pass this case and a Node 22/24 build (Unicode 16.0) would diverge on even more code points.

input.notes:
Only one mismatch exists in the assigned U+3000..U+FFFF range, and it is a symptom of a broader class. The complete set of code points where Node's Unicode 15.1 tables disagree with CPython 3.12's Unicode 15.0 tables is exactly the Unicode 15.1 character additions, and I confirmed every one of them mismatches (each with the same literal-vs-\\u/\\U escape divergence):

  - U+2FFC, U+2FFD, U+2FFE, U+2FFF (Ideographic Description Characters) - BELOW my range, so whoever owns U+2000-U+2FFF should be seeing these. Repro: /tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xe2\xbf\xbc')" --b y --c z
  - U+31EF - reported above, in my range.
  - U+2EBF0..U+2EE5D (CJK Unified Ideographs Extension I, 622 code points) - ASTRAL, so the supplementary-plane dimension should be seeing these; Python emits \U0002ebf0 etc. Repro of the two endpoints: /tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xf0\xae\xaf\xb0')" --b y --c z  and  /tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xf0\xae\xb9\x9d')" --b y --c z
  Boundary code points on both sides (U+2FFB, U+31EE, U+31F0, U+2EBEF, U+2EE5E) all PASS, which pins the cause to the version delta rather than a range/off-by-one bug in the escaping logic.

Everything else in my dimension is byte-identical: quote selection, the \\uhhhh lowercase-hex 4-digit form, the Zs exception for U+0020 only (U+3000 correctly escaped), Co/Cf/Cn/Cs handling, noncharacters, variation selectors, and long-value/error-path formatting. The escaping algorithm in /output/lib/py/repr.mjs (reprStr) is otherwise a faithful match; the only defect is the data source used by isPrintableCodePoint in /output/lib/py/unicode.mjs.

Reproducibility caveat for the maintainer: because the bug is host-Unicode-dependent, the U+31EF repro will only FAIL on a Node whose ICU is Unicode >= 15.1 (verified here on node v18.19.1 / ICU 74.2 / unicode 15.1). It is still a real port defect - the port must not inherit its Unicode version from the runtime.
